what_its_for: This medicine is used to relieve moderate to moderately severe pain. It contains two pain relievers that work together: hydrocodone, which is an opioid (narcotic) pain medicine, and acetaminophen, which is a non-opioid pain reliever that boosts the effect of hydrocodone.
how_to_take: Take this medicine exactly as your doctor prescribed. Swallow the tablet or capsule whole with a full glass of water. You may take it with food or milk if it upsets your stomach. Do not crush, chew, or break the tablets, as this can release too much medicine at once and be dangerous. Never take more than prescribed or take it more often than directed.
dosing: Your doctor will decide the right dose for you based on your pain level and medical condition. The usual adult dose is 1 to 2 tablets every 4 to 6 hours as needed for pain. Do not take more than your prescribed dose, and never exceed 8 tablets per day or the maximum acetaminophen limit of 4,000 mg per day (from all sources combined). Always follow your doctor's specific instructions.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose and you are still in pain, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at the regular time. Never take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one, as this can be dangerous.
storage: Store this medicine at room temperature between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep it out of reach of children and pets at all times. When you no longer need this medicine, dispose of it properly — take it to a drug take-back program or a pharmacy disposal kiosk. Do not flush it down the toilet unless the label says it is safe to do so.
what_to_avoid: Do not drink alcohol while taking this medicine — it can cause serious liver damage and increase the risk of dangerous side effects. Avoid driving, operating heavy machinery, or doing any activity that requires you to be fully alert until you know how this medicine affects you, because it can cause drowsiness and dizziness. Do not take other medicines that contain acetaminophen (such as Tylenol or many cold and flu products) without checking with your doctor or pharmacist, as too much acetaminophen can seriously damage your liver. Avoid taking sleeping pills, anxiety medicines, muscle relaxers, or other opioids without your doctor's approval, as combining these can slow or stop your breathing.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you experience: slow, shallow, or stopped breathing; extreme sleepiness or difficulty staying awake; confusion or unusual behavior; yellowing of your skin or eyes (signs of liver problems); dark urine or severe stomach pain; chest pain; seizures; or signs of an allergic reaction such as hives, swelling of the face or throat, or difficulty breathing. Also call your doctor if your pain is not being controlled, if you feel you need to take more medicine than prescribed, or if you feel dependent on the medicine.
when_it_works: This medicine usually starts to relieve pain within 30 to 60 minutes after you take it. The pain relief typically lasts about 4 to 6 hours. It works best when taken at the first sign of pain, rather than waiting until the pain becomes very severe.
special_populations: Older adults (65 and older): You may be more sensitive to the side effects of this medicine, especially dizziness, drowsiness, and constipation. Your doctor may start you on a lower dose. Pregnancy: This medicine can harm an unborn baby and cause withdrawal symptoms in newborns. Tell your doctor right away if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. Breastfeeding: Hydrocodone can pass into breast milk and may harm a nursing baby. Talk to your doctor before breastfeeding. Children: Safety and dosing in children must be determined by a doctor. Do not give this medicine to a child without a doctor's specific instructions. Liver or kidney disease: Tell your doctor if you have liver or kidney problems, as the acetaminophen in this medicine can worsen liver conditions, and your dose may need to be adjusted.
